obs_height_adjustment.method: neutral log profile over open water
obs_height_adjustment.z0_sensitivity: z0 1.0 m would give 0.769; the open-water value is used because this station's upwind fetch is water through the sectors that matter

truth_exposure: marine — San Pedro breakwater light at the harbour entrance, open ocean through the southern half of the compass
obs_source: NOAA CO-OPS hourly wind (interval=h — the on-the-hour 6-minute sample)
lead_time: short-lead stitched archive; NOT lead-time stratified

models_not_applied.icon_global: MODELS.ICON.mosModel is `icon_eu`, which does not reach the Pacific. The app fetches icon_seamless here, which resolves to icon_global, so the coefficients describe the right forecast — but the lookup key does not match and the correction is NOT applied. Same situation as at san-juan.

slope_policy.why: The rmse-optimal slope at this venue is 0.40-0.77, which corrects a raw 30 kn forecast to 18-27 kn and drops the share of observed >=18 kn hours the forecast warns about from 50-75 % to 0-29 %. ecmwf_ifs025 warned on 0 of 130. A forecast that cannot produce a strong wind is worse than an uncorrected one however good its rmse, so the slope is pinned and only the offsets are fitted.

gfs_hrrr.slope_constrained_why: a is pinned to 1 so the forecast keeps its range; the rmse-optimal slope shrinks the strong-wind tail away. Only the bias, the sector offsets and the diurnal harmonic are fitted.
gfs_hrrr.ols_rejected_because: FAILS the tail bar — keeps 58% of raw's >=18 kn hits (71/122), 24+ err -5.4 vs raw -1.5 kn

seasonal.note: Olympic sailing 2028 and the Transpac start fall in June-September. applyMOS uses these coefficients inside the window and spec.models outside it; A MODEL ABSENT HERE KEEPS THE YEAR-ROUND SET INSIDE THE WINDOW TOO, which is only safe because every year-round correction here was validated across all five held-out years including their summers.
